newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: GOLF-HARRINGTON SMASHES COURSE RECORD TO TAKE LEAD.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-HARRINGTON SMASHES COURSE RECORD TO TAKE LEAD.

text.p: Irishman Padraig Harrington set a course record with a nine under par 63 to take a two shot lead after the second round in the A$1.2 million ($925,000) Heineken Classic on Friday.

Harrington said he had difficulty keeping track of his score as he moved to 11 under par after firing nine birdies in a blemish-free round to beat the previous course record at the tight Vines layout by two shots.
"Nine under par is my best score for a single round," said the 25-year-old Dubliner. "I had trouble counting up how many under par I was. You very rarely get into that zone."
At the halfway stage, Harrington leads with an aggregate score of 133 from New Zealander Frank Nobilo, who moved to nine under with a second round 69.

But South African Ernie Els, the winner of Johnnie Walker Classic in Queensland last Sunday, the opening tournament on the European PGA Tour, just avoided the cut after finishing on level par 144 by adding a 71 to his first round 73.
New Zealander Greg Turner, the overnight leader after equalling the previous course record with a 65, added a 71 to hold third place on eight under.
Compatriot Michael Campbell, Ireland's Paul McGinley, Spaniard Miguel Angel Martin, Australia's Wayne Riley and Katsuyoshi Tomori of Japan were a shot further back in a share of fourth place.
American Fred Couples, another drawcard in a tournament jointly sanctioned by the European and Australasian PGA Tours, led a group of players on six under.
Despite his course record, Harrington, winner of last year's Spanish Open, described his form as "a little bit erratic" after starting the day on two under.
Asked if he felt under pressure as tournament leader, Harrington said: "I have enough on my plate. Not everything is right with my swing, so I have enough to think about."
Scotland's Colin Montgomerie, who is seeking to become Europe's top golfer for a fifth year in succession, was nine shots adrift of Harrington on two under.
